title: spec review: R4 v2: orchestrator/concurrency.py — adaptive concurrency limit 0..hard_max where a coupled cluster caps only its own contribution, independent groups still count, capacity and merge pressure bound the result (AP P13, P11)
spec:
Why: daemon.dispatch fills wave_limit = min(slots, max_wave or slots) (orchestrator/daemon.py:690), so concurrency is always the hard maximum; AP P13 wants a selected concurrency below the cap derived from evidence (coupled group -> 1-2, five independent modules -> higher), AP P11 wants merge pressure to bound it. v2 after spec review T-0569: the coupled-cluster rule caps that cluster's contribution, never the whole wave; the shared-interface bound keys on reason kinds interference.classify actually emits.
What: new pure module orchestrator/concurrency.py; no daemon edits.
- compatible_groups(ready_ids, pairwise_rows) -> list of lists: connected components over rows with level hard or soft (interference.pairwise shape {a, b, level, reasons}); singletons are independent.
- group_contribution(group, pairwise_rows) -> int: 1 when every pair inside the group is hard (any size), 1 when the group has >= 3 members and any hard edge, 1 when any reason kind in the group is same_glob or glob_covers (shared interface surface; "interface" and "migration" kinds are reserved for a future interference extension and documented as such), otherwise 2 for a soft-only group of size >= 2 (soft pairs may run together when capacity allows), 1 for a singleton.
- select_limit(hard_max, ready_ids, tasks, pairwise_rows, priorities, snapshot=None, pressure=None, durations=None, cfg=None) -> {"hard_max", "limit", "reasons": [strings], "tasks_considered", "expected_benefit_s", "groups": [{"members", "contribution", "kind"}]}. Rules appended to reasons when they bind: "no_ready" -> 0; start at hard_max ("hard_max=N"); structural bound = sum of group contributions ("groups=k contributions=m"); a cluster capped to 1 adds "coupled_group:<ids>" or "shared_interface:<ids>"; capacity bound = sum of executor free (claude_workers_free in fallback) ("capacity=m"); pressure saturated -> limit <= max(1, number of singleton groups) ("merge_pressure=saturated"); cfg [scheduler].concurrency_mode fixed|adaptive (default adaptive; fixed -> hard_max with reason "fixed"); minimum 1 when ready work exists and capacity > 0; never above hard_max.
- expected_benefit_s = sum(est durations of the first limit ranked tasks) - max(those), durations dict or critical_path.est_duration_s priors.
- log_row(result, wave_ids=None) -> dict for schedlog.append("concurrency", ...) with hard_max, limit, reasons, tasks_considered, expected_benefit_s, selected, observed_outcome None.
acceptance: tests/test_concurrency.py::test_coupled_cluster_caps_only_its_own_contribution — a hard-coupled cluster of four plus three independent singletons with hard_max 8 yields limit 4 (1 + 3) with reason coupled_group naming the cluster
tests/test_concurrency.py::test_independent_modules_select_higher_concurrency — five ready tasks with no interference and hard_max 4 yield limit 4 and the hard_max reason binds
tests/test_concurrency.py::test_hard_max_is_never_exceeded_and_fixed_mode — twenty independent tasks and hard_max 3 yield limit 3; concurrency_mode fixed returns hard_max with reason fixed
tests/test_concurrency.py::test_no_ready_work_yields_zero — empty ready set yields limit 0 and reason no_ready
tests/test_concurrency.py::test_shared_interface_pair_contributes_one — two tasks whose pairwise reason is same_glob contribute 1 with reason shared_interface

tests/test_concurrency.py::test_quota_and_merge_pressure_bound_the_limit — a snapshot with 2 free executor slots bounds the limit to 2 with a capacity reason; pressure saturated with one singleton bounds to 1 with merge_pressure=saturated; log_row carries hard_max, limit, reasons, tasks_considered, expected_benefit_s

risks.issue: expected_benefit_s = sum(durations of first limit ranked tasks) - max(those) is unguarded for the empty case. limit=0 (no_ready) or any path yielding an empty selected slice makes max() raise ValueError on an empty sequence, which directly breaks acceptance test test_no_ready_work_yields_zero unless the implementer adds a guard the spec never mentions.

The shared-interface rule ('1 when any reason kind in the group is same_glob or glob_covers') is unreachable under default classification: interference.DEFAULT_RULES already places same_glob and glob_covers in the hard bucket, so any pairwise row carrying those reason kinds already has level=hard and is already caught by the 'every pair inside the group is hard' rule. test_shared_interface_pair_contributes_one therefore cannot distinguish this rule from the plain hard-pair rule -- it will pass whether or not the shared-interface branch is implemented at all, so it doesn't verify what the spec claims.

snapshot and pressure parameter shapes (key names like 'claude_workers_free'/'free_slots', and what 'saturated' looks like) are not pinned anywhere in the codebase -- daemon.py's free_slots()/running_claude_workers() use different names, and no 'pressure' concept exists yet. Since this task deliberately makes no daemon edits, tests are free to invent any shape, so acceptance can pass with a contract the eventual daemon-integration spec will have to rewrite.

Reason-kind extraction (splitting a reason string like 'same_glob:pattern' on ':') mirrors interference._reason_kind, which is a private (underscore-prefixed) helper. The spec doesn't say whether concurrency.py may import it or must reimplement the split itself; importing a private symbol across modules is the kind of coupling a reviewer would reject.

suggested_spec_changes: State explicitly that expected_benefit_s must be 0 when the selected slice of ranked tasks is empty (limit 0), before summing/maxing.

Either drop the same_glob/glob_covers shared-interface branch (since it's already covered by the hard-pair rule under default rules) or add an acceptance test that exercises it under a rules override where same_glob/glob_covers are reclassified as soft, so the branch is actually verifiable.

Pin the exact key names/shape expected in snapshot (e.g. {'free_slots': int} or {'claude_workers_free': int}) and pressure (e.g. {'state': 'saturated'} vs a bare string) so the future daemon-integration spec has a fixed contract to match.
Specify that concurrency.py implements its own reason-kind split (reason.split(':', 1)[0]) rather than importing interference._reason_kind.
